A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentAuditor and ASSEBench. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, embedding and label-noise analyses, and human evaluations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds clustering comparisons, adversarial attacks, cross-dataset memory transfer, and retrieval-quality experiments.

M1.justification: The three-stage framework, feature extraction, FINCH selection, CoT generation, and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 and the prompt templates match. Alternative clustering and retrieval configurations are supplementary comparisons.

E1.justification: The datasets, ASSEBench subsets, and represented application categories remain unchanged. Appendix O adds test scenarios involving adversarially compromised evaluator memory and R-Judge memory used to evaluate ASSEBench-Safety and ASSEBench-Security.

E2.justification: V2 adds K-Means, K-Medoids, and DBSCAN as alternatives to FINCH in the clustering comparison in Table 17. The original LLM evaluators, ShieldAgent, Llama-Guard-3, and embedding-model comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The supplementary experiments introduce matched 24-cluster controls, DBSCAN producing 14 shots, specified poisoning rates and exclusion rules, cross-dataset memory construction, and forced retrieval ranks 4–6. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; N=8, K=3, and embedding dimension 512 move from the appendix to Section 5.1.

E4.justification: Appendices N and O substantially expand validation through alternative clustering algorithms, three adversarial attack tiers, cross-dataset transfer, and deliberately poorer retrieval. V1's label-noise experiment remains as O.1. Random retrieval was already tested in Table 2; the forced ranks 4–6 experiment is new.

E5.justification: Both versions retain human-evaluator standard-deviation error bars and Krippendorff's alpha of 0.86. V2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Average poisoned-shot counts are an experimental metric, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 17–20 add substantive results on clustering, attacks, transfer, and retrieval quality. Examples include 84.65 F1 under the Level 3 attack and 86.36 F1 using R-Judge memory on ASSEBench-Safety. Existing benchmark, ablation, resource-use, and human-evaluation results remain unchanged; Table 20 repeats the earlier random-retrieval result.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and algorithms are retained. Scenario, risk-type, and behavior-mode definitions move into Section 4.1. The new scalability discussion supplies informal arguments without adding formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a training-free memory-augmented evaluator, broadly improved evaluation performance, human-level results, and the joint safety/security ASSEBench benchmark. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of component synergy, clustering performance, transfer from imperfect memory, and scalability. Existing limitations move to Section 6. Its new assertion that few-shot prompting alone underperforms is unsupported by Table 2: the no-CoT few-shot configuration scores 83.74 F1 and 83.33 accuracy versus baseline values of 82.27 and 81.21.

D1.justification: The repository pointer changes from AgentAuditor-ASSEBench to AgentAuditor. V2 documents parameters for the new clustering comparisons and clarifies that resource analysis focuses on LLM costs because PCA and FINCH costs are considered negligible. Existing hardware, deployment details, prompts, and default retrieval settings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references, including MedSentry, WebCloak, and Agent-as-a-Judge. These modestly broaden citations around agents and evaluation; the existing CoT/RAG discussion and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 gains structure/construction subsections, definitions and limitations move into the main text, and Appendix A and the ablation explanation are revised. Author-affiliation and conference-header text also changes. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds four appendix tables, numbered 17–20; the former resource-use and human-comparison tables become 21–22. Existing figures retain their content, while tables and figures undergo limited relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added clustering, poisoning, transfer, and retrieval experiments strengthen validation beyond v1's component and label-noise studies. Bringing definitions and limitations into the main text also improves accessibility. The net gain is limited by the added experiments' single-backbone scope and the new ablation interpretation's conflict with Table 2.
